A Clear and Simple Learning Journey How Personalized Tutoring Works at Success Path Mentors From understanding the student's needs to measuring progress, every stage is organized to provide clear, consistent, and personalized academic support. Five structured steps A Learning Process Built Around the Student We do more than schedule lessons. We identify the student's needs, select the right tutor, build a focused plan, and adjust support as progress develops. A learning plan based on the student's current level and goals One-to-one lessons with a tutor suited to the student's needs Clear follow-up and practical updates throughout the program Book a Free Trial No long-term commitment is required to begin. Tell Us About the Student 01 Share the student's grade, subject, learning goals, current challenges, preferred language, and suitable lesson times. Assess the Current Learning Level 02 We review the student's needs and identify strengths, learning gaps, and the skills that should receive priority. Match the Student with the Right Tutor 03 We select a qualified tutor based on the subject, curriculum, grade level, learning needs, and preferred teaching language. Begin Personalized Lessons and Follow-Up 04 The student begins one-to-one lessons supported by focused practice, feedback, and homework follow-up when appropriate. Monitor Progress and Refine the Plan 05 We follow the student's development, communicate relevant updates, and adjust priorities as academic needs change. Personalized Support at Every Step A Complete Learning Experience Designed Around Every Student From private lessons and curriculum support to progress reporting, homework follow-up, and flexible scheduling, every service is designed to help students learn with clarity, confidence, and consistency. Personalized academic support Support That Continues Beyond Every Lesson Every lesson is connected to a clear learning goal, with structured follow-up, practical feedback, and ongoing communication to support steady academic progress. Parent Communication Clear updates on learning progress Flexible Scheduling Lessons arranged around student availability Ask About a Free Trial Private One-to-One Online Tutoring 01 Each student learns individually with a qualified tutor who adapts the lesson to their level, pace, learning style, and academic goals. Canadian and American Curriculum Support 02 Lessons are aligned with Canadian and American curricula, helping students understand key concepts, strengthen subject knowledge, and prepare for different assessment formats. Clear Progress Reports 03 Parents receive practical updates on the student's strengths, areas for improvement, completed work, and recommended next steps. Homework and Lesson Follow-Up 04 Students receive focused practice after lessons when appropriate, with follow-up and feedback to reinforce understanding and address learning gaps. Focused Exam Preparation 05 Students practise important concepts and a variety of question formats while developing the confidence and problem-solving skills needed for exams. Flexible Lesson Scheduling 06 Lesson times are arranged around the student's availability, making it easier for families to maintain a consistent and manageable learning routine. Personalized Learning Plan 07 We create a clear learning plan based on the student's current level, academic goals, priority skills, and progress throughout the tutoring program. Why Families Choose Success Path Mentors A Focused Response to the Learning Challenges Families Face Every learner faces different obstacles. Our approach combines individual teaching, appropriate tutor matching, structured follow-up, and flexible scheduling to provide support that fits the student. 01 Lessons That Move Too Quickly Common challenge Students may struggle when classroom explanations move forward before they fully understand the previous concept. Our approach The tutor adjusts the pace, explanation, examples, and practice to match the student's current understanding. 02 Learning Gaps That Build Over Time Common challenge Missing foundational skills can make new lessons more difficult and gradually reduce confidence. Our approach We identify priority gaps and include the necessary foundational skills within a clear and focused learning plan. 03 Difficulty Finding the Right Tutor Common challenge A tutor may understand the subject well but may not match the student's curriculum, language, or learning style. Our approach Tutor selection considers the subject, grade, curriculum, preferred language, and the student's individual learning needs. 04 Limited Visibility for Parents Common challenge Families may not always know what the student is learning, where progress is occurring, or what still needs attention. Our approach Parents receive practical communication and relevant updates about learning priorities, completed work, and recommended next steps. 05 Schedules That Are Difficult to Maintain Common challenge School, family responsibilities, and time-zone differences can make regular tutoring difficult to organize. Our approach Online lessons are arranged around student availability to support a consistent and manageable learning routine. 06 Low Confidence and Learning Motivation Common challenge Repeated difficulty can make students hesitant to participate, ask questions, or attempt challenging work. Our approach One-to-one lessons provide a supportive environment where the student can ask questions, practise, and progress without classroom pressure. Not Sure Where the Student Should Begin? Tell us about the student's grade, subject, current challenges, and learning goals. We will help identify a suitable starting point. Contact us through WhatsApp and share the student's grade, subject, curriculum, preferred teaching language, current learning challenges, and available times. Our team will review the information and help arrange the appropriate next step. 02 Is the trial lesson free? A free trial lesson may be arranged for eligible new students before beginning a regular package. The purpose is to understand the student's needs, introduce the tutoring experience, and help determine an appropriate tutor and starting point. 03 How is the tutor selected? Tutor selection considers the subject, grade level, curriculum, preferred teaching language, student availability, and individual learning needs. The goal is to provide a suitable match rather than assigning the same tutor profile to every student. 04 How long is each lesson? Lesson duration can vary according to the student's age, subject, program, and selected arrangement. The exact lesson duration is confirmed with the family before regular lessons or package payment begins. 05 Are lesson times flexible? Yes. Regular attendance is encouraged to support consistent progress. 06 Which subjects and curricula are available? Success Path Mentors supports a range of subjects including Mathematics, English, Science, Physics, Chemistry, French, Arabic, and other available programs. Support may include Canadian, American, Quebec, and other curricula depending on the grade, subject, and available tutor. 07 Can we request a different tutor? The situation will be reviewed and an alternative tutor may be considered based on availability. 08 How is the student's progress followed? Progress may be followed through lesson feedback, completed work, priority skills, homework follow-up when applicable, and communication with the family. The level of reporting depends on the student's program and tutoring arrangement. 09 What happens if a lesson needs to be rescheduled or cancelled? Families should contact the team as early as possible when a lesson cannot be attended. Rescheduling, cancellation, late-notice, and missed-lesson conditions are confirmed before payment and are handled according to the applicable policy. 10 How are package payments handled? Package prices are shown in Canadian dollars. Before payment, the family should confirm the number and duration of lessons, payment method, applicable taxes, renewal arrangements, and the relevant cancellation or refund conditions. h1: Personalized tutoring built around each student

A student-centred approach supported by clear standards
One-to-one support that adapts to the student
A structured matching and follow-up process
Tell us what your student needs help with
rows.text: Skip to main content Home About About Success Path Mentors Personalized tutoring built around each student Success Path Mentors, operated by Success Path Mentors, provides one-to-one online tutoring designed around the student’s subject, grade, learning goals, schoolwork, and preferred schedule. Explore our tutoring approach Email our team Grades 1–12 Academic support across elementary, middle, and high school. One-to-one lessons Individual attention rather than a large group format. Family communication Clear coordination around schedules, needs, and progress. Our purpose Making high-quality academic support easier to access Students learn differently, and the support they need can change from one subject, grade, or school term to another. Success Path Mentors was developed to give families a more flexible and personal alternative to one-size-fits-all tutoring. Our lessons take place online, allowing students to learn from home while receiving direct support from a tutor matched to the subject and learning need. The goal is not simply to complete a worksheet or provide an answer. Our approach focuses on explaining concepts, identifying gaps, practising skills, improving confidence, and helping the student become more independent over time. We also recognize the important role of parents and guardians. Clear scheduling, practical communication, and appropriate follow-up are part of creating a stable learning experience. What guides us A student-centred approach supported by clear standards Our decisions are guided by educational value, professional communication, and a practical understanding of what families need from an online tutoring service. Student first The lesson begins with the student’s current level, learning goal, and immediate academic need. Clear learning goals Tutoring should have a defined purpose, whether that is strengthening foundations, preparing for an assessment, or improving a specific skill. Professional communication Families should receive respectful, understandable, and timely communication about scheduling and learning needs. Responsible academic support Tutors guide students through schoolwork and skill development without replacing the student’s own effort. Thoughtful tutor matching Subject knowledge matters, but communication style, grade level, language, availability, and student fit matter as well. Continuous improvement Feedback from students, families, tutors, and supervisors helps improve lesson quality and operations. How learning works One-to-one support that adapts to the student Our model is designed to make the lesson relevant to the student’s real school experience rather than following a fixed script for every learner. Individual attention The tutor can adjust the pace, explanations, examples, and practice to one student. Curriculum-aware support Families can share the student’s grade, school material, assignments, and curriculum context so lessons stay relevant. Skill building Lessons can address immediate work while also strengthening the underlying knowledge needed for future progress. Tutor quality and fit A structured matching and follow-up process A successful tutoring relationship depends on both academic capability and the student’s ability to understand and communicate comfortably with the tutor. 01 Understand the student We collect the grade, subject, learning goal, preferred language, schedule, and any relevant school information. 02 Select an appropriate tutor The matching decision considers subject knowledge, teaching experience, communication, availability, and the student’s needs. 03 Review and adjust Families can provide feedback after lessons. When a different approach or tutor is needed, the team reviews the situation and coordinates the next step. Common questions About the academy Key information for families considering personalized online tutoring. 01 What grades does Success Path Mentors support? The academy provides tutoring support for students in Grades 1–12. Available subjects and tutors can vary by grade, curriculum, language, and schedule. 02 Are lessons private or group-based? The core service is one-to-one online tutoring, allowing the tutor to focus on one student’s academic needs and learning pace. 03 Can lessons follow the student’s school curriculum? Families can share the student’s grade, school material, assignments, and curriculum information. The tutor can then align explanations and practice with the material the student is currently studying. 04 Can a family request a different tutor? Yes. Tutor fit is important. A parent or guardian can contact the team to explain the concern, and the academy will review the request and coordinate an appropriate next step based on availability. 05 Does the tutor complete homework for the student? No. Tutors can explain concepts, demonstrate methods, review attempts, and guide the student through the work. The student remains responsible for completing and submitting their own assignments. Start with a clear learning goal Tell us what your student needs help with Share the grade, subject, preferred schedule, and current learning challenge. Our team can use that information to guide the next step. View tutoring options Email the academy

rows.text: Skip to main content Home Cancellation and Rescheduling Policy Scheduling policy Cancellation and Rescheduling Policy This policy explains how cancellations, absences, rescheduling requests, late arrival, tutor cancellations, and technical problems affect lesson balances and recurring schedules. August 5, 2026 Last updated Trial lessons, package lessons, and recurring online tutoring schedules unless a specific written exception applies Applies to successpathmentors@gmail.com Contact email 1. Purpose of this policy Tutors reserve lesson times and prepare in advance. This policy is intended to support continuity for students, respect tutor time, and give families a clear and consistent process for schedule changes. A booking confirmation, invoice, package description, promotion, or written agreement may contain additional terms. A more specific written term applies when it addresses the same issue, subject to mandatory consumer rights. 2. Meaning of a calendar week For this policy, a calendar week normally runs from Monday through Sunday using the time zone recorded for the student, unless the academy confirms a different arrangement in writing. 3. How to request a cancellation or schedule change A parent or guardian should send the request through an approved academy communication channel before the scheduled lesson begins. Telling the tutor alone may not complete the request unless the academy or an authorized scheduling administrator confirms it. The request should identify the student, tutor, lesson date and time, and the requested action. A schedule change is not final until the academy confirms it. A package, booking, or written offer may establish a longer advance-notice period. That requirement applies when it was clearly communicated before the lesson or package was confirmed. 4. One eligible cancellation and reschedule per week Unless a different written arrangement applies, one lesson for the same student may be cancelled and requested for rescheduling during a calendar week. The replacement lesson should normally be completed during the same calendar week. It remains subject to tutor, classroom, and schedule availability, and a requested replacement time is not guaranteed. A rescheduling request does not extend a package expiry date unless the academy confirms an extension in writing. 5. Second cancellation or absence during the same week A second cancellation, missed lesson, or student absence during the same calendar week will normally be counted as a used lesson and deducted from the student’s balance. This rule normally applies even when the family asks to move the lesson to a later week, unless the academy approves an exception based on the circumstances. 6. Minimum weekly attendance and continuity A student with an active recurring schedule is expected to attend at least one lesson during each calendar week unless the academy has approved a pause, holiday arrangement, or exceptional absence. Repeated interruption may affect tutor availability, the reserved recurring time, learning continuity, package administration, or the ability to maintain the same schedule. 7. No-shows and late arrival A lesson is considered missed when the student does not join and the academy has not confirmed a cancellation or reschedule. The tutor is not required to extend the lesson beyond the scheduled ending time when the student joins late. The tutor may wait for a reasonable period while the team attempts contact. The lesson may still be counted from the scheduled start time. Repeated late arrival or absence may result in a schedule review or release of a reserved recurring time. 8. Cancellation by the tutor or academy When the tutor or academy cancels a lesson, the lesson will not be deducted as a completed student lesson. The academy will normally offer a replacement time, restore the lesson to the balance, coordinate an available substitute where appropriate, or apply another reasonable correction. The academy will make reasonable efforts to communicate the change. To the extent permitted by law, it is not responsible for indirect costs resulting from a scheduling change. 9. Technical problems Problem on the student’s side The family is responsible for a functioning device, stable internet connection, audio, browser or application, platform access, and joining information. A problem limited to the student’s device, connection, login, or local environment does not automatically create a free replacement lesson. Problem on the tutor or academy side When a material technical failure controlled by the tutor or academy prevents the lesson from being delivered, the academy will review the circumstances and may reschedule, restore time or credit, or otherwise adjust the lesson. Reporting a technical problem The family should notify the team as soon as the problem occurs and provide a brief description or screenshot when practical. Delayed reports may be harder to verify. 10. Emergencies and exceptional circumstances The academy may consider a documented emergency, serious illness, bereavement, widespread outage, severe weather event, displacement, or another exceptional circumstance on a case-by-case basis. An exception is not automatic and does not create a permanent waiver of this policy. The academy may request reasonable supporting information while avoiding unnecessary sensitive details. 11. Planned holidays and temporary pauses Families should provide advance notice for known travel, examinations, school holidays, or temporary pauses. A pause may affect the recurring time and tutor assignment. Holding a tutor’s time during an extended pause is not guaranteed unless confirmed in writing. Package validity and payment obligations continue according to the applicable package terms unless the academy confirms otherwise. 12. Changes to a recurring schedule Requests to change a recurring day or time are subject to tutor availability. The academy cannot guarantee that the original tutor will be available at the new time. The academy may review or release a recurring time when attendance is inconsistent, payment is overdue, communication is not maintained, or the schedule is repeatedly changed. 13. Lesson balances, packages, credits, and refunds A cancellation or rescheduling request does not automatically create a cash refund. Lessons are administered according to this policy, the package terms, the payment record, and any specific written refund arrangement. Used, missed, expired, promotional, complimentary, or discounted lessons may be non-refundable to the extent permitted by applicable law and the written terms accepted by the customer. When the academy verifies an attendance or lesson-balance error, it may correct the record by restoring a lesson, applying credit, rescheduling, issuing an eligible refund, or making another reasonable adjustment. The family should contact the academy and allow a reasonable opportunity to review attendance, balances, and communications before initiating a payment dispute, except where urgent legal action is reasonably necessary. 14. Trial and complimentary lessons Trial, complimentary, promotional, and discounted lessons may be subject to separate eligibility, expiry, rescheduling, and one-per-student or one-per-family conditions. A missed trial or complimentary lesson may be considered used and may not be replaceable when a tutor reserved the time and the academy did not confirm a timely cancellation. 15. Review and decisions The scheduling or administration team may review attendance records, messages, platform information, payment records, and the circumstances reported by the family and tutor. A one-time exception does not require the academy to make the same exception again. Decisions remain subject to applicable consumer law and any written agreement. Questions or review requests can be sent to successpathmentors@gmail.com. 16. Mandatory consumer rights Nothing in this policy removes a cancellation, refund, disclosure, or other consumer right that cannot legally be waived. Where the law gives a customer a right that is more favourable than this policy, the mandatory legal right applies. 17. Changes to this policy The academy may update this policy to reflect scheduling practices, service changes, package structures, or legal requirements. The revised version will show an updated date. Changes do not retroactively remove rights that cannot legally be waived. Need help with a schedule change? Send the student name, tutor, lesson date and time, and the requested change. A request is complete only after the academy confirms it. successpathmentors@gmail.com

rows.text: Skip to main content Home Data Deletion Instructions Privacy request Data Deletion Instructions This page explains how a parent, guardian, student, tutor, website visitor, or Meta user can request deletion of personal information held by Success Path Mentors. August 5, 2026 Last updated Website, tutoring, account, inquiry, communication, payment-administration, and Meta-connected data Applies to successpathmentors@gmail.com Contact email 1. How to request deletion Send an email to successpathmentors@gmail.com with the subject line “Data Deletion Request.” Use the email address or telephone number previously used with the service when reasonably possible. This helps us locate the correct records and protect information from unauthorized deletion requests. State your full name and your relationship to the student or account. Identify the student, account, inquiry, telephone number, email address, or Meta profile connected with the request. Describe whether you want all eligible data deleted or only specific records. Do not send passwords, full payment-card numbers, government identification, or unnecessary sensitive documents by ordinary email. 2. Requests connected with Facebook, Instagram, or Meta If you used a Meta product to contact us, log in, submit a lead form, or connect with an app, you may request deletion using the same email process above. Include the relevant Meta profile name or app interaction and the approximate date. Where Meta sends us a platform data-deletion request or signed request through an enabled callback, we will process the request using the identifiers supplied by Meta and provide the confirmation information required by the platform. Deleting information held by us does not automatically delete information held independently by Meta. You may also need to use the privacy and account controls offered by Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, or another Meta service. 3. Identity and authority verification Before deleting information, we may take reasonable steps to confirm the requester’s identity and authority. For a student who is a minor, the request should normally come from the parent, guardian, or authorized adult who arranged the service. Verification is limited to what is reasonably necessary. We may ask for confirmation from an existing contact channel or for non-sensitive details already associated with the account. 4. What we will delete or de-identify Eligible contact, inquiry, profile, scheduling, communication, educational, lesson-support, and Meta-connected records under our control. Files or materials supplied for tutoring when they are no longer required for an active service, legal obligation, safety matter, complaint, or dispute. Information in active systems, followed by removal from backups according to normal backup rotation where immediate deletion is not technically practical. Aggregated or de-identified information may be retained when it no longer identifies the person. 5. Information we may need to retain Deletion is subject to applicable law and legitimate recordkeeping needs. We may retain limited information where reasonably necessary to: Complete an active transaction, refund, chargeback, accounting, tax, or payment obligation. Maintain invoices, financial records, consent records, safeguarding records, or proof that a request was completed. Investigate fraud, security, abuse, safety concerns, complaints, or legal claims. Establish, exercise, or defend legal rights, comply with a court order, or meet another legal obligation. Maintain a minimal suppression record when needed to honour a do-not-contact or deletion preference. 6. Timing and confirmation We will acknowledge a reasonably complete request and aim to complete eligible deletion without undue delay. Timing may vary where identity must be verified, records must be located across service providers, or law requires retention. When the request is completed, we will provide confirmation or explain any limited information that must be retained and the reason for retention. 7. Requests concerning children and students We treat student information as sensitive. A parent or guardian may request access, correction, or deletion of a minor student’s information, subject to identity verification, the student’s evolving capacity where applicable, and legal recordkeeping requirements. Children under 13 should not independently submit website forms or deletion requests. A parent, guardian, or authorized adult should contact us on their behalf. 8. Questions or complaints Questions, complaints, or concerns about a deletion request may be sent to successpathmentors@gmail.com. Please include “Privacy Complaint” in the subject line. You may also have the right to contact the privacy or consumer-protection authority that applies in your jurisdiction. rows.title: How Online Tutoring Works | Success Path Mentors
rows.description: See how Success Path Mentors learns about the student, matches an appropriate tutor, coordinates the schedule, and supports ongoing one-to-one online learning.
h1: A clear path from the first request to ongoing tutoring
headings: The family does not have to navigate the process alone
How a student begins with Success Path Mentors
A few details help make the first session more useful
The tutor teaches, guides, and checks understanding
The plan can continue, improve, or change
Share the student’s needs and preferred schedule
rows.text: Skip to main content Home How It Works How it works A clear path from the first request to ongoing tutoring We begin by understanding the student’s grade, subject, curriculum, learning goal, preferred language, and availability. The team then coordinates an appropriate tutor and a suitable lesson time. View the six-step process Learn about our team Student information first The matching process begins with the student’s real academic need. Thoughtful tutor matching Subject knowledge, grade, communication, language, and availability are considered. Review and adjustment Families can share feedback and request a review when the fit needs to change. Simple and guided The family does not have to navigate the process alone Our team coordinates the main steps: collecting the student’s information, reviewing the request, selecting an available tutor, confirming the schedule, and following up after the first lesson. Step by step How a student begins with Success Path Mentors The process is designed to stay practical and transparent while giving the team enough information to make a responsible tutoring match. 01 Share the student’s details Provide the grade, subject, curriculum or school system, preferred language, learning goal, and available times. 02 Clarify the learning need The team reviews whether the student needs foundational support, homework guidance, exam preparation, skill development, or help with a specific topic. 03 Match an appropriate tutor The tutor is considered according to subject knowledge, experience with the grade level, communication style, language, and schedule. 04 Confirm the lesson time The family and our team confirm a suitable lesson time and the family receives the information needed to join the online lesson. 05 Complete the first lesson The tutor begins by understanding the student’s current level, explaining the target concept, and observing how the student responds to the teaching approach. 06 Review and continue The family can provide feedback. When the fit is suitable, the team coordinates the ongoing schedule and package. When changes are needed, the request is reviewed. Before the first lesson A few details help make the first session more useful The more accurately the family describes the student’s current situation, the easier it is to prepare a relevant lesson and choose an appropriate tutor. Grade, subject, and curriculum Share the student’s current grade and the curriculum, province, state, country, or school program when known. Current material When helpful, send the topic, textbook pages, assignment, teacher notes, or upcoming assessment information before the lesson. Availability and time zone Provide more than one suitable time when possible and confirm the family’s time zone to avoid scheduling confusion. During the lesson The tutor teaches, guides, and checks understanding A one-to-one lesson allows the tutor to adjust explanations and practice to the student rather than delivering the same lesson to a large group. Explain the concept The tutor breaks the topic into understandable steps and uses examples suited to the student’s level. Guide active practice The student is encouraged to think, answer, solve, read, write, or explain rather than only watch the tutor. Check understanding The tutor asks questions, reviews attempts, identifies errors, and adjusts the pace when the student needs more support. After the lesson The plan can continue, improve, or change The first lesson is also an opportunity to review tutor fit, communication, pace, and the student’s response before confirming the next stage. Family feedback A parent or guardian can share comments about the lesson, scheduling, communication, or the student’s experience. Ongoing schedule When the fit is suitable, our team coordinates the agreed lesson frequency and confirms the applicable package or payment arrangement. Tutor or plan adjustment When the approach, time, or tutor is not suitable, the team reviews the request and coordinates an available alternative where possible. Common questions Starting and continuing lessons Answers to practical questions families often ask before beginning online tutoring. 01 What information should I provide before the first lesson? Please provide the student’s grade, subject, curriculum or school system, learning goal, preferred language, time zone, and suitable times. Relevant assignments, textbook pages, or assessment information can also help the tutor prepare. 02 How is the tutor selected? The team considers the requested subject, grade level, curriculum context, language, teaching experience, communication style, availability, and the information provided about the student. 03 Is the first lesson an assessment? The first lesson can include informal observation of the student’s level and needs, but it is also a real teaching session. The exact format depends on the subject, grade, and goal. 04 What happens if the tutor is not a good fit? A parent or guardian can contact our team and explain the concern. The team will review the feedback and coordinate a reasonable next step based on tutor availability and the circumstances. 05 How often should the student attend? The suitable frequency depends on the student’s goal, current level, school workload, and available schedule. Consistent attendance generally supports continuity, but the final schedule is agreed with the family. 06 Can the tutor help with homework and exams? Yes. The tutor can explain concepts, guide practice, review the student’s work, and support preparation. The tutor does not complete graded work or take an assessment on behalf of the student. Begin with the right information Share the student’s needs and preferred schedule Tell the team the grade, subject, learning goal, language, time zone, and available times. This gives us a clear starting point for the tutoring request. View tutoring options About Success Path Mentors

rows.title: Privacy Policy | Success Path Mentors
rows.description: Learn how Success Path Mentors and Success Path Mentors collect, use, protect, retain, and share information relating to families, students, tutors, and website visitors.
headings: 11. Access, correction, deletion, and privacy choices
rows.text: Skip to main content Home Privacy Policy Privacy and data Privacy Policy This policy explains how Success Path Mentors, operated by Success Path Mentors, handles information connected with the website, tutoring inquiries, lesson coordination, payments, communication, and educational services. August 5, 2026 Last updated Website visitors, parents, guardians, students, tutors, and service contacts Applies to successpathmentors@gmail.com Contact email 1. Who we are Success Path Mentors is an online tutoring service operated under Success Path Mentors. In this policy, “we,” “us,” and “our” refer to the organization responsible for the relevant website or tutoring service. Privacy questions and requests can be sent to successpathmentors@gmail.com. 2. Scope of this policy This policy applies to information collected through our website, inquiry and contact forms, email, messaging, scheduling, online tutoring, lesson records, payment administration, support, and related operations. External classroom, video, payment, email, cloud, scheduling, analytics, and communication providers may have their own privacy policies. Families should review the terms of services they use. 3. Information we may collect Parent, guardian, and contact information Name, email address, telephone number, WhatsApp number, country, city, time zone, and preferred communication method. Relationship to the student and authority to arrange tutoring or provide consent. Messages, inquiries, complaints, feedback, and customer-support records. Student and educational information Student name or first name provided by the family, age or age range, grade, school year, curriculum, subject, course, language preference, availability, and learning goals. Assignments, worksheets, textbook pages, school comments, assessment dates, academic concerns, and work shared for tutoring. Lesson attendance, scheduling history, tutor notes, progress observations, recommendations, and family feedback. Information about accommodations, learning preferences, or an individual education plan when a parent or guardian chooses to share it. Payment and transaction information Package selected, amount, currency, payment status, invoice information, credits, adjustments, refunds, and transaction references. Payment-card details are normally handled by the payment provider rather than stored directly by us, except for limited information required for administration and accounting. Website and technical information IP address, browser, device, operating system, referring page, pages visited, approximate location, date and time, cookie identifiers, and security logs. Information submitted through website forms, including submission time and anti-spam information. Audio, video, and lesson recordings Online lessons may involve live audio, video, chat, screen sharing, whiteboards, and uploaded files. We do not treat recording as a standard lesson requirement. When recording is proposed for a stated purpose, appropriate notice or consent will be requested where required. Third-party classroom platforms may process technical session information under their own terms. 4. How we use information Respond to inquiries and recommend an appropriate next step. Match students with tutors according to subject, grade, curriculum, language, availability, and learning needs. Schedule, deliver, administer, and support online tutoring lessons. Communicate with parents, guardians, students where appropriate, tutors, administrators, and supervisors. Process payments, issue invoices, maintain balances, and respond to financial questions. Review lesson quality, tutor fit, attendance, complaints, safety concerns, and service performance. Protect accounts, investigate misuse, prevent spam and fraud, and maintain website and system security. Comply with legal, accounting, tax, insurance, contractual, safeguarding, and dispute-resolution obligations. Improve services, website content, and operations using information that is aggregated, de-identified, or otherwise permitted by law. 5. Children, consent, and parental authority Our services are frequently arranged for children and teenagers. Website inquiry and payment forms are intended to be completed by a parent, guardian, or authorized adult rather than independently by a child. A parent, guardian, or authorized adult should approve service terms, arrange payment, and provide required consent when the student cannot provide meaningful consent independently. We do not knowingly collect personal information online directly from a child under 13 without the involvement or authorization required from a parent or guardian. A child under 13 should not submit a website form or create a service request independently. The adult arranging tutoring confirms that they have authority to provide the student information and permissions required for the service. Families should not submit unnecessary identity documents, card numbers, passwords, immigration records, medical records, or other highly sensitive information through the website or ordinary email. Student information is treated as sensitive and should be limited to what is reasonably needed for tutoring, scheduling, progress support, safety, payment administration, or legal obligations. We do not use student information for targeted advertising, and we do not knowingly sell student or child personal information. A parent or guardian may request access, correction, or deletion of a minor student’s information, subject to identity verification, legal retention requirements, and the student’s evolving capacity where applicable. 6. When information may be shared We do not knowingly sell personal information. We may share information only when reasonably needed for the purposes described in this policy. With the tutor, supervisor, administrator, or staff member who needs it to coordinate or deliver the service. With providers supporting hosting, classrooms, video, email, cloud storage, scheduling, analytics, customer support, payments, accounting, and security. With professional advisers, insurers, accountants, payment providers, or legal representatives where reasonably necessary. With a school, agency, or other person when the parent or guardian authorizes the disclosure or law permits or requires it. With regulators, courts, law enforcement, or other authorities when legally required or reasonably necessary to protect rights, safety, students, staff, systems, or the public. In connection with a lawful merger, financing, reorganization, sale, or transfer of the business, subject to confidentiality and legal requirements. 7. International processing Because tutoring is delivered online and families, tutors, and providers may be located in different countries, information may be processed or stored outside the person’s province, state, or country. Information processed in another jurisdiction may be subject to the laws and lawful-access rules of that jurisdiction. We take reasonable steps to select and manage providers appropriate to the service and information involved. 8. Retention and deletion We retain information only as long as reasonably necessary for the purpose for which it was collected and for legitimate legal, tax, accounting, payment, quality, safety, complaint, and dispute-resolution needs. Retention periods vary by record type. Inquiry messages may be retained for follow-up, while transaction and invoice records may need to be kept longer. When information is no longer required, we take reasonable steps to delete, anonymize, or securely dispose of it, subject to backup cycles and legal restrictions. Detailed instructions for submitting a deletion request are published at /en/data-deletion and /ar/data-deletion. Requests may also be sent to the contact email shown on this page. 9. Security safeguards We use administrative, technical, and organizational safeguards intended to protect information against loss, theft, unauthorized access, disclosure, copying, use, or modification. No internet, email, video, or storage system is completely secure. Families should protect devices and login information, avoid publishing lesson links, and report suspected unauthorized access promptly. 10. Cookies, analytics, and embedded content The website may use essential cookies and similar technologies for language selection, security, forms, performance, and basic functionality. Analytics or marketing technologies should be used only with the notice or choice required by applicable law. Embedded content, including video providers, may receive technical information when content loads or is played. Browser settings and available consent controls can be used to manage certain cookies. 11. Access, correction, deletion, and privacy choices Depending on applicable law, an individual or authorized parent or guardian may request access to information, ask for inaccurate information to be corrected, withdraw consent, object to certain uses, or request deletion. We may need to verify identity and authority before responding. Some records may be retained or withheld when permitted or required by law, including information related to payments, legal claims, safety, another person’s privacy, or confidential business information. Requests may be submitted to successpathmentors@gmail.com. Please describe the person involved, the type of record, and the requested action without sending unnecessary sensitive identification documents. 12. Service and promotional communications We may send communications needed to respond to an inquiry, coordinate lessons, confirm schedules, administer payments, provide support, or communicate a policy or service change. Promotional electronic messages will be sent only as permitted by applicable law. They should identify the sender and provide an appropriate unsubscribe method. Necessary service communications may continue while tutoring is active. 13. Privacy incidents and complaints We review suspected privacy or security incidents and take steps appropriate to the circumstances. Where required, we may notify affected individuals, providers, regulators, or authorities. A privacy concern or complaint can be sent to successpathmentors@gmail.com. We may request information needed to verify identity, understand the issue, and respond. 14. Changes to this policy We may update this policy when services, technology, providers, business practices, or legal requirements change. The revised version will show a new last-updated date. When a change is significant, we may provide additional notice or request new consent where required. Privacy questions Contact the academy to ask about information, request access or correction, or report a privacy concern. successpathmentors@gmail.com

h1: The right tutor is more than a subject match
headings: Knowing the subject is essential, but it is not the only factor
Useful information helps us make a more responsible match
From the student request to the first lesson
A real teaching session and an opportunity to review fit
Tutor fit can be reviewed without blaming the student or tutor
What tutor matching does and does not guarantee
Share the student’s subject, goal, language, and schedule
rows.text: Skip to main content Home Tutor Matching Tutor matching The right tutor is more than a subject match We consider the student’s grade, curriculum, learning goal, preferred language, schedule, communication needs, and the tutor’s relevant experience before coordinating the first lesson. See the matching criteria How tutoring works Academic fit Subject knowledge, grade level, curriculum context, and the student’s current need. Communication fit Language, explanation style, patience, pace, and student comfort. Practical fit Time zone, tutor availability, lesson frequency, and continuity. Why fit matters Knowing the subject is essential, but it is not the only factor A strong tutoring relationship also depends on whether the student can follow the explanation, ask questions comfortably, participate actively, and attend lessons consistently. Academic understanding The tutor should understand the requested subject and be able to teach at the student’s grade and course level. Clear communication The tutor should explain ideas in language and steps the student can understand and apply. Goal alignment The teaching approach should match the goal, whether it is foundational support, homework guidance, exam preparation, or skill development. What we learn first Useful information helps us make a more responsible match Families do not need to prepare a formal assessment. Clear practical details about the student are enough to begin the review. Grade and subject The student’s current grade, requested subject, course name, and the exact topic when known. Curriculum or school context The province, state, country, school program, course code, textbook, or current school material when relevant. Language preference The preferred teaching language and whether bilingual explanation may support understanding. Learning goal The immediate challenge and the result the family hopes to achieve through tutoring. Availability The family’s time zone, suitable days, preferred times, and expected lesson frequency. Learning considerations Any communication preferences, school feedback, attention needs, or accommodations the family chooses to share. Our matching process From the student request to the first lesson The process is designed to balance timely coordination with a reasonable review of academic, communication, and scheduling fit. 01 Review the request The team checks the grade, subject, learning goal, curriculum, language, schedule, and any material shared by the family. 02 Identify available tutors The team reviews tutors who can support the subject and grade and whose availability is compatible with the family’s time zone. 03 Compare academic and practical fit Relevant teaching experience, communication, language, schedule, and the student’s stated needs are considered together. 04 Confirm the proposed match The family receives the proposed lesson arrangement and the information needed to confirm the first session. 05 Complete the first lesson The tutor begins teaching while observing the student’s level, pace, communication, and response to the lesson. 06 Continue or adjust When the match works, the schedule continues. When a reasonable change is needed, the team reviews available alternatives. The first lesson A real teaching session and an opportunity to review fit The first session helps turn the information provided by the family into a clearer understanding of the student’s academic level, communication needs, and next priority. Observe the current level The tutor reviews how the student approaches the topic, responds to questions, and applies previous knowledge. Review communication The lesson shows whether the explanation style, language, pace, and interaction are understandable and comfortable. Clarify the next priority The tutor and family gain a clearer view of the skill, topic, or study plan that should receive attention next. When a change is needed Tutor fit can be reviewed without blaming the student or tutor A tutor may be capable and professional but still not be the best fit for a particular student, schedule, language preference, or learning goal. Share specific feedback Explain whether the concern relates to communication, pace, teaching style, schedule, subject coverage, or another practical issue. Allow the team to review The academy may clarify the concern, review lesson information, and determine whether an adjustment or different tutor is appropriate. Coordinate an available alternative When a change is approved, the team searches for a suitable available tutor. A particular tutor or exact time cannot always be guaranteed. Important expectations What tutor matching does and does not guarantee The academy works to make a thoughtful match, but tutoring outcomes depend on several factors beyond tutor selection. The academy does not guarantee a specific tutor, exact schedule, grade improvement, examination score, or academic result. Tutor availability can change because of time zones, school terms, illness, emergencies, or changes in the tutor’s schedule. Families should provide accurate information and timely feedback so the team can review the match responsibly. Students are expected to attend prepared, participate respectfully, and complete their own schoolwork. A tutor change request is reviewed in good faith and remains subject to availability and the applicable cancellation and scheduling rules. Common questions Questions about tutor matching Practical information about selection, the first lesson, preferences, and requesting a change. 01 Can I choose a specific tutor? You can share preferences or request a tutor you already know, but assignment depends on subject fit, availability, schedule, and the academy’s review. A specific tutor cannot be guaranteed. 02 How quickly can a tutor be matched? Timing depends on the subject, grade, language, time zone, requested schedule, and current tutor availability. Providing several suitable times can make coordination easier. 03 Can I request a male or female tutor? Families may share this preference. The academy will consider it together with subject requirements, schedule, and tutor availability, but cannot guarantee every preference. 04 What if the student has an IEP or learning accommodation? A parent or guardian may share relevant information that will help the tutor communicate and plan appropriately. Tutoring is educational support and is not a substitute for medical, psychological, diagnostic, or specialized therapeutic services. 05 Can we change the tutor after the first lesson? Yes. A parent or guardian can request a review. The team will consider the reason, the lesson experience, and available alternatives before coordinating the next step. 06 Does tutor matching guarantee better grades? No. The academy cannot guarantee a specific grade or result. Progress depends on attendance, participation, practice, school requirements, the student’s starting point, and other factors. Help us make a better match Share the student’s subject, goal, language, and schedule The more clearly the request describes the student’s current need, the easier it is to review academic, communication, and practical fit. View tutoring options How tutoring works

Évaluation de la compétence en français
Choisir le bon point de départ
rows.text: Aller au contenu principal Programme entièrement en français Français et mathématiques enseignés en français Une carte curriculaire structurée de la 1re à la 12e année, avec domaines, sujets principaux, sous-sujets, compétences visées et activités pédagogiques. Explorer le français Explorer les mathématiques matières 2 domaines curriculaires 10 années scolaires 1re–12e sous-sujets publics 640 Références externes Ressources sur le DELF et la compétence en français Consultez ces ressources de conseils scolaires pour mieux comprendre les évaluations de compétence en français et le DELF. Les critères, l’admissibilité et les dates peuvent varier selon le conseil scolaire et l’année. Évaluation de la compétence en français Waterloo Catholic District School Board (WCDSB) Informations d’un conseil scolaire ontarien sur les évaluations de compétence en français et l’admissibilité des élèves. Examens du DELF District School Board of Niagara (DSBN) Présentation du Diplôme d’études en langue française, des niveaux évalués et du contexte offert aux élèves du secondaire. Diplôme d’études en langue française (DELF) Simcoe County District School Board (SCDSB) Renseignements sur les niveaux du CECR, les quatre compétences évaluées et la sélection du niveau DELF approprié. Ces liens sont fournis à titre de référence. Vérifiez toujours les exigences actuelles auprès de l’école ou du conseil scolaire concerné. Deux parcours complémentaires Choisir la matière Chaque matière possède sa propre page, ses domaines et ses pages curriculaires organisées par niveau. 4 domaines Français Un parcours complet de littératie couvrant la communication orale, les notions fondamentales de la langue, la compréhension et la rédaction. Liens et mise en application en littératie Notions fondamentales de la langue Compréhension des textes Rédaction et création de textes Ouvrir le parcours 6 domaines Mathématiques en français Un parcours de mathématiques enseigné entièrement en français, de la numération aux fonctions, aux données, à la géométrie et à la littératie financière. Processus mathématiques Nombres Algèbre Données Sens de l’espace Littératie financière Ouvrir le parcours Structure pédagogique Une carte claire et exploitable Chaque parcours présente une progression claire par niveau, avec les compétences et les activités utiles pour guider l’apprentissage. 1 Niveau 2 Domaine 3 Sujet principal 4 Sous-sujet 5 Compétence visée 6 Activité pédagogique Accompagnement personnalisé Choisir le bon point de départ Indiquez le niveau de l’élève, la matière et les objectifs. L’équipe pourra proposer un parcours et un enseignant adaptés. Réserver un cours d’essai

rows.description: Planification, organisation, rédaction, révision, correction et création de différents genres de textes.

rows.title: Mathématiques en français par niveau | Success Path Mentors
rows.description: Un parcours de mathématiques enseigné entièrement en français, de la numération aux fonctions, aux données, à la géométrie et à la littératie financière.
rows.text: Aller au contenu principal Parcours du Programme français Mathématiques en français Un parcours de mathématiques enseigné entièrement en français, de la numération aux fonctions, aux données, à la géométrie et à la littératie financière. Explorer les domaines Réserver un cours d’essai domaines 6 sous-sujets 315 années couvertes 1re–12e Carte curriculaire Domaines de Mathématiques Ouvrez un domaine pour consulter les sujets principaux, les sous-sujets, les compétences et les activités par niveau. 12 niveaux Processus mathématiques Résolution de problèmes, raisonnement, communication, modélisation, codage et consolidation des stratégies. 47 sujets principaux 57 sous-sujets Ouvrir le domaine 10 niveaux Nombres Sens du nombre, opérations, fractions, décimaux, pourcentages, rapports, proportions et estimation. 59 sujets principaux 92 sous-sujets Ouvrir le domaine 12 niveaux Algèbre Régularités, expressions, équations, relations, fonctions, polynômes et raisonnement algébrique. 41 sujets principaux 45 sous-sujets Ouvrir le domaine 12 niveaux Données Collecte, représentation, analyse et interprétation des données, probabilités et statistiques. 33 sujets principaux 36 sous-sujets Ouvrir le domaine 11 niveaux Sens de l’espace Géométrie plane et dans l’espace, mesure, transformations, coordonnées, angles, aires et volumes. 52 sujets principaux 72 sous-sujets Ouvrir le domaine 12 niveaux Littératie financière Argent, budget, décisions financières, taux, intérêts, coûts, revenus et planification financière. 13 sujets principaux 13 sous-sujets Ouvrir le domaine
